subject: Post-call recap: ACME - TCO & next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: ACME - TCO & next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to understand ACME's usage profile and goals. Below is a concise recap, the cost levers we discussed, and proposed next steps. I copied Monica (Solutions Eng) and Marissa (Finance/Sales ops) to help with the TCO worksheet and procurement timeline.

1) Key pain points you shared
- Per-token spend is high and unpredictable: current vendor billed ~ $14k/mo for inference (fluctuates by traffic).
- Peak latency spikes affecting UI during bursts — want 95th pctile < 300ms.
- Large embedding batch volume for search (~500k vectors/month) plus ~20M generation tokens/month.
- Budget constraint: target ~ $7k/mo for inference to start (pilot).

2) Goals / success criteria
- Reduce monthly inference cost by ~40–60% while keeping output quality; target pilot budget $6–8k/mo.
- Maintain 95th latency < 300ms for interactive flows.
- Validate quality regression <= 3% on your evaluation prompts.

3) Cost/TCO levers we reviewed (how Redwood helps)
- Batching: dynamic batching and request-level batching reduces per-token overhead for high QPS flows. For your profile, batching alone can cut costs ~20–35% depending on QPS distribution.
- Prefix/KV caching: repeated prefixes (e.g., system prompts or shared context) can be cached — big win for chat-heavy workloads with repeated templates.
- Model selection & quantization: moving from a large 16-bit model to an instruction-tuned 4-bit quantized variant frequently reduces cost 30–50% with small quality loss for many prompts. We can run evals on your test set.
- Embedding optimizations: batching and mixed-precision kernels reduce vector compute; consider async bulk embeds for nightly jobs.

4) Ballpark economics (based on numbers you gave)
- Current: ~20M gen tokens/mo + 500k embed vectors = ~ $14,000/mo (vendor invoices).
- Redwood projected (pilot config with batching + caching + 4-bit quantization): ~ $5,800–7,200/mo (estimated 45% savings).
- Detailed line items in attached TCO worksheet (acme-tco-worksheet.xlsx). These are estimates — we'll run a short PoC to validate.

5) Risks / trade-offs
- Quantization: small accuracy delta possible; we recommend AB tests on your critical prompts.
- Caching: only safe for deterministic prefixes and non-personalized secrets — we'll review which contexts are cacheable.

6) Action items / next steps
- Rafael: deliver TCO worksheet and one-pager on batching/caching (attached) — TODAY.
- Monica: schedule a 60-min PoC kickoff and review sample prompts + test data — proposed times below.
- Sarah: share a small sample set of ~50 representative prompts, recent invoices (aggregated monthly totals), and a note on compliance requirements (SOC 2 / data residency) by EOD Wednesday.

Proposed PoC times (Monica): Wed 6/24 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 6/25 9:00–10:00 PT — what works best?

Attachments: acme-tco-worksheet.xlsx (TCO by lever), redwood-batching-cache-one-pager.pdf (short explainer).

If helpful I can also pull a 7–14 day simulated run on Redwood to validate the estimate before the PoC.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
redwood.ai

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T14:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ACME - TCO & next steps

Thanks Rafael — really appreciate the fast follow-up and the clear list. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Budget: our procurement can approve ~ $7k/mo for a pilot (3 months). Anything materially higher will need additional sign-off.
- Tokens: the 20M number is a steady average; we get spikes up to ~45M in peak weeks (launches). Need to see how batching behaves on spikes.
- Accuracy: we cannot tolerate quality drops > ~3% on our top 20 intents; willing to try quantized models if we can validate.
- Security: we require SOC 2 Type II and will need an overview of data retention and logging for the pilot.

We'll bundle the 50 representative prompts and last 3 months' invoices and upload to a private Drive link by EOD Wednesday.

Quick Q: does prefix caching ever change the observable output for users (e.g., if cache returns a slightly older KV state)? We have some personalized tokens in prompts so I want to understand safety.

Also, Monica — hi — can you join the PoC kickoff if we pick Wed 6/24 10am PT?

—
Sarah
Senior Product Manager | ACME Corp
sarah.lee@acme.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: ACME - TCO & next steps

Thanks Sarah — great questions. Short answers below, plus next steps and proposed schedule.

On caching safety:
- Prefix/KV caching is deterministic: we cache the model's internal KV for identical prefixes/contexts only. It does not return "older" or unrelated state for distinct prompts. For prompts that include user-specific tokens, we recommend scoping the cache to shared system prompts and templates, not per-user secrets. Monica will help identify which parts of your prompt are cache-friendly during the kickoff.

On spikes and batching:
- Redwood's dynamic batching adapts to QPS; batching efficiency improves with higher QPS, so spikes actually increase batching opportunities (up to a point). We also support autoscaling policies to keep latency SLOs during launches. We'll model a spike scenario in the TCO worksheet.

On quantization and quality:
- 4-bit quantization (our standard path) generally shows minimal quality drop on instruction-tuned models for many intents — but we always recommend running your top-20 intent eval. We'll run a paired AB test and surface objective deltas. If needed, we can route high-sensitivity prompts to a larger model and low-cost prompts to the quantized variant (routing by intent).

Updated ballpark (see attached worksheet): with batching + caching + 4-bit quantization we estimate ~$5.8k/mo for steady-state 20M tokens; factoring peak-week spikes and a conservative safety margin puts us at ~$7.2k/mo for the pilot — which looks aligned to your $7k cap.

Next steps:
- Monica to schedule PoC kickoff (60 min). Proposed: Wed 2026-06-24, 10:00–11:00 PT. Monica, can you confirm?
- Sarah: upload prompts + aggregated invoices + security checklist link by EOD Wed.
- Rafael/Monica: run evaluated AB test on the 20-key intents within 5 business days of kickoff and share report.

Attachments: acme-tco-worksheet.xlsx (populated with your numbers), redwood-batching-cache-one-pager.pdf
Links: https://redwood.app/sales/ACME-2026-001 (deal page)

If Wed 10am PT doesn't work, here are alternate slots: Thu 6/25 9:00–10:00 PT or Fri 6/26 11:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to the PoC.
